newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ NOTCHES 10TH COMPLETE GAME FOR EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ NOTCHES 10TH COMPLETE GAME FOR EXPOS.

text.p: Pedro Martinez hurled a three-hitter for his major league-leading 10th complete game to carry the Montreal Expos to a 6-3 victory over the San Diego Padres on Sunday.
Doug Strange and Darrin Fletcher each hit two-run homers in a six-run fifth inning for the Expos, who took three of four games in the series.
Martinez (13-5) allowed three runs -- one earned -- with three walks and 10 strikeouts for his third complete game in five starts as he lowered his league-leading ERA to 1.76.
After struggling a bit early, Martinez retired 17 straight batters before Ken Caminiti led off the ninth with a home run.

"He got in a rhythm, he's one of the best pitchers in the game," Padres manager Bruce Bochy said. "We got a break early with a couple of unearned runs. But he's as tough as there is, he can flat out pitch."
Andy Ashby (6-8) held the Expos scoreless the first four innings before falling apart in the fifth.

Mark Grudzielanek led off with a single and Strange followed with his seventh home run to tie it at 2-2. The Expos scratched out two more runs before Fletcher sent Ashby's 3-1 pitch over the right-field wall to cap the six-run outburst.

In Chicago, Sammy Sosa's two-out, two-run homer into the left-field bleachers off closer Todd Worrell in the bottom of the 12th inning lifted the Cubs to a dramatic 4-3 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Sosa tied the game in the eighth with an RBI double after Raul Mondesi's second solo homer of the game had put the Dodgers ahead 2-1 in the seventh.

The Dodgers went in front again in the top of the 12th on Greg Gagne's solo homer to centre. But with Mark Grace on base and the Cubs down to their last out, Sosa hit a hanging breaking ball for his 23rd homer to end the contest.
In Cincinnati, Darryl Hamilton's RBI single with one out in the top of the 10th inning ignited a five-run explosion as the San Francisco Giants beat the Reds 8-3.
Hamilton's single off reliever Jeff Shaw snapped a 3-3 tie. Barry Bonds added an RBI double and J.T. Snow capped the inning with a two-run, ground-rule double.
Roberto Hernandez (1-0), the fourth Giants pitcher, tossed two scoreless innings to earn his first National League win.
Shaw, who had allowed just 10 earned runs all season, was charged with all five runs on four hits and two walks.
At Florida, Devon White had four hits and three RBI to lead the Marlins to an 8-4 victory over the Atlanta Braves.
White singled and scored in the first inning, added a two-run single and scored in the second, doubled in the third and had an RBI single in the fifth.
"This was a great series," Florida manager Jim Leyland said after his team won three of four to close within 5 1/2 games of the Braves in the East. "This weekend we took a big step forward."
Alex Fernandez (13-8) allowed four runs and seven hits in eight innings and struck out 10. Kevin Millwood (2-3) was torched for seven runs and eight hits in three innings.
In Houston, Craig Biggio hit a two-run homer in the seventh and scored the winning run in the ninth as the Astros edged the New York Mets 3-2.
Todd Hundley gave the Mets to a 2-0 lead in the first with a towering homer off Shane Reynolds. Biggio tied it with his two-run shot off reliever Juan Acevedo in the seventh.
With two out in the ninth, Biggio singled to right against Greg McMichael (7-9), who walked the next two batters before hitting Luis Gonzalez to force in the winning run.
Tom Martin (4-2) got the win with two scoreless innings.

In Philadelphia, Mark Leiter pitched a complete-game seven-hitter and Kevin Sefcik and Scott Rolen homered in a five-run third inning that propelled the Phillies to a 10-1 rout of the St Louis Cardinals.
Rookie Tony Barron went 4-for-4 with a pair of doubles and three runs scored for the Phillies.
Leiter (7-11) allowed a run and walked one with six strikeouts. Donovan Osborne (1-4) was ripped for eight runs and seven hits in three-plus innings.
In Pittsburgh, Kevin Polcovich had a two-run double and Tony Womack added a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning that lifted the Pirates an 8-4 win over the Colorado Rockies.
Womack had his second four-hit game in eight days for the Pirates, who took three of four from Colorado.
Colorado grabbed a 4-3 lead on Larry Walker's RBI single in the seventh, but Pittsburgh scored five times in the eighth off relievers Steve Reed (3-5) and Curtis Leskanic.
Matt Ruebel (3-2) picked up the win in relief.
